title: Biology Paper 2 practice paper
subtitle: Kuphanda mock paper — 100 marks, 2 hours. Written for practice; not a MANEB examination.

blocks.text: Answer all questions. Write your answers in the spaces provided. The paper carries 100 marks and you are advised to spend 2 hours on it. Show your working where a calculation is needed.
A student placed a piece of potato in distilled water and another piece of the same size in a strong sugar solution. Both were left for 30 minutes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what happened to the mass of each piece of potato.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain each result in terms of water movement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Name the process responsible and state two ways it differs from diffusion.

blocks.text: The graph shows the rate of photosynthesis of a water plant at different light intensities, at 20 degrees Celsius and at 30 degrees Celsius.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the effect of light intensity on the rate up to the point where the graph levels off.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the graph levels off at high light intensity.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest why the rate at 30 degrees is lower than at 20 degrees at high light intensity.

blocks.text: In cattle, the allele for black coat (B) is dominant to the allele for red coat (b).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: A heterozygous black bull is crossed with a red cow. Use a Punnett square to show the possible offspring.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the expected ratio of black to red offspring.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why a black offspring cannot be described as pure-breeding without further testing.

blocks.text: The table shows the number of fish caught in a lake over five years while the number of fishing boats doubled.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the trend in the catch over the five years.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest two reasons for the trend, other than the number of boats.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Recommend two measures a fisheries department could take, and explain each.

blocks.text: The diagram shows a section through the human heart.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Name the four chambers and the two main vessels entering the heart.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the path of blood from the vena cava to the aorta.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why the wall of the left ventricle is thicker than that of the right.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: State two ways the structure of a vein differs from that of an artery, and relate each to its function.

blocks.text: A farmer clears a slope beside a river to grow maize. Within three seasons the maize yield falls and the river becomes muddy after every storm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain how clearing the slope led to soil erosion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe two effects of the muddy river on organisms living in it.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Suggest three soil-conservation measures the farmer could use, and explain how each works.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why the yield continued to fall even after the farmer applied more fertiliser.
